title: Delhi Tops Global Affordability, Mumbai Leads India in QS Student City Rankings
excerpt: Delhi earned the highest affordability score among 150 cities, while Mumbai climbed to 91st globally in the QS Best Student Cities 2027 rankings.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Delhi scored 93.9, making it the world's most affordable student city with $2,700 tuition.
  • Mumbai improved to 91st globally, leading Indian cities with strong employer activity and affordability.
  • Four Indian cities ranked: Mumbai (91st), Delhi (99th), Bengaluru (joint 114th), Chennai (123rd).
  • Seoul remains the top global student city, followed by Tokyo, London, and Melbourne.

Delhi has been named the world's most affordable student city in the QS Best Student Cities 2027 rankings, while Mumbai emerged as India's highest-ranked education destination overall. The rankings, released on Tuesday by London-based higher education analysts QS Quacquarelli Symonds, evaluated 150 cities worldwide on factors shaping the student experience.

Delhi Earns Top Global Affordability Score

Delhi scored 93.9 in the affordability category — the highest recorded among all 150 cities in this year's rankings. The national capital's average annual international tuition fee stands at around US$2,700, making quality higher education comparatively accessible for both domestic and international students.

The city also advanced in the overall rankings, climbing from 104th in 2026 to 99th in 2027 with a composite score of 60.3. Delhi ranked 29th globally for employer activity, reflecting healthy demand for graduates among recruiters and industries.

"The combination of affordable education and promising career opportunities helped Delhi strengthen its position in the global rankings."

— QS Best Student Cities 2027 Report

Mumbai Enters Global Top 100

Mumbai recorded the strongest performance among Indian cities, improving its position from 98th in 2026 to 91st in the 2027 edition, with an overall score of 61.8. The city scored 78.3 in employer activity, reflecting a robust graduate employment market. It also secured 84.4 in affordability, ranking 12th globally on that metric.

Mumbai's remaining indicator scores included 44.9 for desirability, 43.5 for student view, 39 for university rankings and 15 for student mix. According to QS, the city's rise was driven largely by strong employment opportunities and cost-effectiveness for students, according to the Telegraph India.

![Mumbai. Mumbai improved to 91st globally, leading Indian cities with strong employer activity and affordability.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)

Chennai Improves, Bengaluru Slips

Chennai and Bengaluru also featured in the 2027 rankings. Chennai climbed to 123rd from 128th in 2026, continuing its upward trajectory. Bengaluru, however, slipped to joint 114th from 108th the previous year.

Bengaluru recorded the highest average international tuition fees among the four Indian cities at around US$5,400 per year, according to the Times of India. Despite the rankings dip, the city remains home to institutions such as the Indian Institute of Science and continues to attract students drawn to India's technology capital.

Seoul Leads Globally, Asian Cities Dominate Top Spots

At the global level, Seoul retained its position as the world's best student city. Tokyo secured second place, followed by London in third. Melbourne ranked fourth, while Munich and Sydney jointly occupied fifth position. Paris, Berlin, Vienna and Zurich rounded out the top 10.

Among other major Asian destinations, Singapore ranked 11th, Beijing secured 12th place and Kuala Lumpur was placed 15th — underscoring Asia's growing strength as a higher education hub.

What the Rankings Mean for Indian Students Abroad — and at Home

The QS rankings assess cities across six broad parameters: university quality, employer activity, affordability, desirability, student mix and student view. These categories are measured through 23 indicators using QS survey data and independent third-party sources. Cities must have a population exceeding 250,000 and host at least two QS-ranked universities to qualify.

For Indian students considering options domestically versus studying abroad, the rankings reinforce a shifting calculus. With tuition and living costs rising sharply in traditional study-abroad destinations like the United States, United Kingdom and Australia, Indian cities' affordability advantage is increasingly relevant. Delhi's US$2,700 average annual tuition compares favourably against fees that can run 10 to 20 times higher at universities in the US or UK.

For NRI families evaluating where their children should pursue higher education, the rankings offer data-backed reassurance that Indian cities are climbing in quality and employability — not just affordability. Mumbai's 34th-place global ranking in employer activity signals that graduates from its universities are increasingly competitive in the job market.
